leverage.exposure: The balance is negative and must be back to non-negative, with at least eleven players, before the matchday locks. It is not yet close, and the deficit costs nothing in the meantime. The position unwinds with a single sale that is already decided, leaving a small positive balance and a legal eleven, so there is no scenario here that requires a scramble. The two flips, if both win, add to the deficit temporarily, but each sells back to Kickbase at the market value on demand and neither reduces the fielded eleven, so they do not change the unwind picture. The one thing that would make this urgent is drift: if the sale is left to the final hours and something goes wrong with it, there is no second leg that clears the deficit on its own. That is the argument for executing inside the stated window rather than against the lock itself.

binding_gap: A third attacker. The squad carries only two, one of them flagged, and the sale that clears the deficit removes a defender, which narrows the legal formations further. The gap cannot be closed this run because every attacker on the board fails the unwind ceiling, and it does not need to be closed before the lock as long as the flagged attacker is fit, which the dated news says he will be. It becomes urgent only if that changes.

verdict.detail: No action is required today, and that is the finding rather than a shrug. The leveraged position is open but the lock is still more than eight days out, a negative balance costs nothing until the instant it locks, and the single sale that clears it is already identified and unconditional. What this run adds is the timing: that sale should NOT be executed yet. Treu is on the rising side of the daily tick and selling back to Kickbase pays the market value exactly, so every night he is held is free money, and selling him today would throw away a meaningful fraction of the deficit for no benefit at all. The rule is now anchored to the lock rather than to tonight, so no future run has to re-derive it: hold him until after the last tick before the lock, then sell inside the window that follows.

sell.reason: Treu remains the sole unwind leg and the case is unchanged on merit: he is a fit, confirmed starter, listed in his club's probable eleven, and he is being sold purely because he is the most expensive point in the fielded eleven by some distance. What changed is WHEN. He is on the rising side of the tick, the sell-back price is the market value with no spread, and there are several ticks left before the lock. Selling early is a pure loss. The sale should happen after the final tick before the lock and before the lock itself. Three things would break that rule and nothing else: his trend flag flipping to falling, an approved purchase that needs the cash sooner, or an injury. The alternative of selling the flagged attacker instead was re-checked and is worse, because it forces the floor-priced defender into the eleven and gives up more fielded average than it saves.

standing.name: Philipp Treu
standing.why: REPLACES S3a3aqf, WHOSE TIMING LEG WAS A ONE-NIGHT INSTRUCTION ("not today, hold through tonight's tick"). That expires tonight and would leave the next run re-deriving the same question from scratch every six hours. This converts it into a STATE RULE that needs no re-derivation. WHETHER: unconditional and unchanged. He is the sole unwind leg for cash -10.773.918. EXHAUSTIVE RE-CHECK OF THE ALTERNATIVES FROM LIVE DATA 2026-09-30T14:45Z, so no future run repeats it: only Treu 12.818.870, Gregoritsch 12.624.784, Neuer 12.567.324, Deman 10.806.960, Gruber 10.311.240, Nusa 27.856.915 and Guirassy 32.663.839 individually exceed the debt. Neuer is the only GK. Nusa/Guirassy break the front line and are the two best assets. Gregoritsch alone clears it and leaves a legal 5-4-1, but at 1243 fielded ap. Deman (-74) and Gruber (-90) both cost more points than Treu and Gruber does not even clear the debt alone. Treu costs -49 (XI 1353 -> 1304, Nakuzola ap 27 replaces him) and is the cheapest legal unwind that exists. WHEN — THE STATE RULE: sell to Kickbase at exactly mv on the FIRST run that observes him at mvt 2, and otherwise HOLD while he stays mvt 1. Grounds: measured next-tick drift this run is mvt 1 n=613 mean +2,42% with 86,8% rising, against mvt 2 n=525 mean -3,52% with only 10,5% rising, so every 20:00Z tick held while mvt 1 is worth ~+310.000 at his current mv and every tick held after the flag flips costs ~-450.000. Holding is points-free: there is NO matchday before the 2026-10-09T18:30Z lock, the 11-player floor is checked once at matchday start (Hn0qy58), and selling during the Laenderspielpause costs nothing (Hfbknqv, Georg 23.09). He is mvt 1 right now with sdmvt +635.239 and tfhmvt +7.105. HARD DEADLINE: gone before 2026-10-09T18:30:00Z whatever the flag says, because a negative balance at matchday start scores ZERO for the whole matchday (~1304 fielded ap). THE ONLY CANCELLER is the balance reaching non-negative by other means, which nothing on this account currently does. NOTE THE TFHMVT WEAKNESS HONESTLY: tfhmvt is only +7.105 against sdmvt +635.239, so his rise has nearly flattened in the last few hours and the flag may flip within a tick or two — this is exactly why the rule is stated as a state test rather than a fixed date.

buy.reason: Nothing on this board is both affordable and an upgrade, and the briefing will not pad that. The binding gap is a third attacker, and the two attackers who could fill it both fail the unwind test rather than the merit test: one is far outside the ceiling that two non-destructive sales can cover, and the other is a near miss on money and a clear downgrade on scoring average, bought only as insurance against an absence the news says will not happen. The genuinely interesting name is a defender whose average would be the best outfield figure in the squad outright and whose price per point beats everything else listed. His fitness was checked and is fine. He fails only on sequencing: because the deficit is pre-existing, swapping him for Treu leaves the balance roughly where it started and forces a second sale that costs more in fielded average than the swap gains. He is recorded as a standing target with an explicit reversal: if cash arrives from anywhere and cuts the deficit to near nothing, he becomes a clean, large upgrade funded by a single sale and should be taken at the market value immediately.

He is the single most tempting listing available: ap 165 would be the HIGHEST in Georg's squad, above Nusa 169's only rival Guirassy 161, and he is a nominee for Bundesliga Player of the Month for September 2026 (bundesliga.com) with ph 126/129/321/85, i.e. four scoring matchdays and no blanks. FIRST, AVAILABILITY: get_player 2030 returns st 256, stl [256], stxt "Personal reasons - absent from team training", dt 2026-09-29T12:00:00Z — dated the day before this run, so it is current, not stale. A personal-reasons absence carries NO published return date and no medical timeline to reason from, which makes it strictly worse to underwrite than an injury; ligainsider.de/phillip-tietz_7480 read this run carries nothing dated later than 07.09.2026 ("Fischer lobt Sturmduo"), so there is no source resolving the absence either way — write it as "no current info found" rather than inferring he is fine. The ask has also sat since 2026-09-29T18:59:38Z unsold, which per doctrine is an invitation to offer at mv, not to pay the ask. REVERSAL: require ALL of (1) st back to 0; (2) a dated Mainz source of 01.10.2026 or later confirming he has returned to team training AND a probable XI that starts him — absence of news resolves AGAINST him, because the absence itself was never explained; (3) an ask at or below mv, since a +13,74% markup on a 19M asset is 2,66M of pure premium and Georg optimises points per euro of a capped envelope; and (4) genuine unwind capacity, because at 22.000.000 he alone more than doubles the current deficit and Treu's 12.821.410 would no longer cover it.

(1) HE CANNOT BE UNWOUND, WHICH IS THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY BINDS. Manager ask from Borussia Rumpelfuss, listed 2026-09-30T15:05:56Z, prc 15.000.000 against mv 12.580.331. (2) EVEN AT mv HE IS POINTS-NEGATIVE, WHICH IS THE SURPRISE AND THE REASON TO LOG IT. (3) THE PRICE IS OUTSIDE EVERY MEASURED BAND ANYWAY. +19,24% over mv on a MANAGER ASK, against a measured manager-to-manager clearing band of +3,06% to +4,35%, widened only to +6,62% by the Stiller clear (H53duk0). That is roughly 3x the top of the band, and a manager ask is seller's choice, not an auction, so there is no contest to lose by refusing. Nothing above +6,62% has ever cleared manager-to-manager in this league.

REVERSAL: require ALL of: the ask AT OR BELOW mv; the squad at 13 or more so his purchase does not consume two fielded bodies; and a recomputed fielded-ap delta that is POSITIVE after counting whoever actually funds him. Being ap 144 is NOT a reversal - that was already true when he was killed.

movers.reason: Both open flips still qualify and both are still priced at exactly the market value, which is the correct bid. The structural point this run adds is that both listings expire AFTER tonight's update, so both auctions resolve while the bids sit at the pre-update price. That is a feature, not a defect, and the next run must not fix it. The edge in this trade is entirely the gap between what you pay and the value that applies when you sell back. Winning at tonight's post-update price closes that gap to nothing and leaves you merely holding for the following night at the usual odds. Winning at the pre-update price means owning a player whose value is already higher, realisable instantly on sell-back with no overnight risk. The lower chance of winning is the correct price for that, and losing an auction costs nothing. So: leave both bids exactly where they are and do not raise them after the update. Separately, the board itself has gone quiet. Every board purchase that settled in the last twelve hours cleared at or barely above the market value, several of them below it, against a recent run of contested clears far above. That is a property of contested listings, not of board listings as such, and right now nothing is being contested. It argues for placing at the market value rather than skipping, and never for bidding above it.

fitness.sweep: Both flagged squad players were checked on dated 2026 sources and neither is a matchday problem. The attacker's ankle knock is real and was correctly identified as live by the previous run, but the scan was clean, there is no structural damage, and his recorded return date has already arrived with well over a week still to run before the match. A date trap was caught and logged in the process: the top organic result for the obvious German query is a club article about his return to training that is actually from 2021 and concerns a completely different absence. The defender's knee irritation is the softer case, still on an individual programme at the most recent dated update, with a prior report that his availability was not considered at risk; there is a long gap before the match and he is being watched rather than acted on. The player being sold was also checked and is a confirmed starter, which matters because it means the sale is a price decision, not a fitness one.
